chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about one who does not recite Fātiḥat al-Kitāb in his salat (prayer). He said: There is no salat (prayer) for him unless he recites it, whether aloud or quietly.

So the proper way regarding this narration is that we interpret it as applying to one who deliberately did not recite it, not one who forgot. For indeed, he has no salat (prayer), according to what we have explained in the earlier reports, and what follows further clarifies that.

key_terms.إِخْفَاتٍ: quiet or inaudible recitation in prayer
key_terms.النِّسْيَانِ: forgetfulness, as opposed to intentional omission
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), the ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, the opening chapter recited in salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does deliberately not reciting Fātiḥat al-Kitāb invalidate salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that reciting Fātiḥat al-Kitāb in salat (prayer) is necessary, and that omission invalidates the prayer when done deliberately. The closing statement explains that the narration is to be understood as referring to intentional abandonment, not forgetfulness, in harmony with the earlier reports.
